status: RENDERED LOCALLY, NOT UPLOADED. This plan is for the next take, not yet recorded. Its content opens on Android TV emulator footage from CI run 37475795991: the debug APK built at f423ba5 on an AOSP Android TV emulator, Android 14 / API 34, loading the public demo (build ea2cff5, record-only), at 1x. That is footage, not a Fire TV device and not a runtime receipt; the Android TV emulator runtime receipt is a separate file, android_tv_runtime_receipt.json. The rest is a local run of this repository in desktop Chromium at 1920x1080 with MERCURY_OFFLINE=1, driven through the D-pad bridge the Leanback app calls. An emulator beat's seconds are its footage window; a desktop beat's seconds are its measured hold, the length of its synthesized audio plus a 0.65 s tail, from video/generate-narration.py. The media lives outside the repository; video/README.md says where. The event FAQ permits the Android TV Emulator and does not require physical hardware.
title: Mercury: Fire TV incident board
note: words_count and words_per_minute are computed from narration_text by the generator. duration_sec is the beat's hold in the render: for an android_tv_emulator beat its window of the CI footage, for a desktop_capture beat the measured audio length plus a 0.65 s tail. total_duration_sec is the content only; the title card (4 s) and the closing card (3 s) are added by video/build-video.py.

beats.narration_text: From the home screen, the debug A P K starts on an Android TV emulator and loads the public demo.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage, 1.00 s to 8.60 s of journey.mp4 at 1x: the Leanback home screen, then black while the app cold-starts and its WebView loads the demo.

beats.narration_text: The board answers: checkout A P I at twelve point nine times baseline.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage, 8.60 s to 14.32 s: the end of the cold start, the board appears, CHECKING, then checkout-api 12.9x, TEMPORAL CANDIDATE, Commit 4f1c2ab from the demo's invented deploy feed, then all five rows.

beats.narration_text: Right, then center stages a rollback. Its lease counts down.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage, 14.32 s to 19.32 s: D-pad Right to Stage rollback, Center. Rollback staged, the lease counting down from 300 s.

beats.narration_text: Right, center confirms: recorded, no pipeline contacted, record only. Center publishes the handoff.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage, 19.32 s to the end at 27.64 s: D-pad Right to Confirm, Center. RECORDED, no pipeline contacted, held on the board; then Center on Publish handoff and the shared handoff, SHARED REVISION 13, HTTP 200.

beats.narration_text: The rest is the same board, run locally in a desktop browser at ten eighty p, so each answer can be read. Mercury counts only commits that touch runtime files, and names one only when exactly one landed before the spike.
beats.visual_action: The desktop take begins: the loaded board at 1920x1080, focus on Ask what changed. No key pressed.

beats.narration_text: It answered on load, before any key was pressed. Most answers are refusals: on generated cases held out from tuning, it saw a real anomaly and named nobody ninety percent of the time. A refusal never calls the deploy innocent.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the board. The five rows read Temporal candidate, Nothing to revert, Cannot attribute, Cannot attribute and Insufficient data, each from the server's answer.

beats.narration_text: Down walks the rows. Release train shows a spike well above its baseline, but several runtime changes landed in the window before it, and no metric says which one did it. Mercury cannot attribute this, and offers no rollback. Rolling back would be a guess.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Down four times to release-train, then Center. The verdict reads Cannot attribute this with the number of changes that landed, Next reads No rollback offered, and Stage rollback and Confirm are disabled.

beats.narration_text: On checkout A P I, exactly one runtime change landed before the spike, so Mercury names it, and prints its own odds: on held-out generated cases a named commit is the cause fifty percent of the time, over fifty eight namings, if a fault shows within seventy five minutes.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Up three times to checkout-api, then Center. The verdict names the commit as the only runtime change, quotes its message, and reads 50.0% held-out precision (synthetic, ≤75m lag).

beats.narration_text: The reading and the commit each carry a stamp. The metric is an offline fixture, generated locally. The commit is one of Mercury's own, standing in for a deploy feed.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the OFFLINE FIXTURE stamp under the reading and the dashed STAND-IN stamp against Mercury's commits. No key pressed. (The public demo in the emulator footage names a deploy from an invented feed instead.)

beats.narration_text: Up, right, center stages the rollback; right, center confirms it, and the board holds recorded, not sent. Center publishes the handoff. Down reaches the evidence behind the odds: fifty eight namings, in eleven hundred sixty synthetic cases.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Up, Right to Stage rollback, Center: Rollback staged. Right to Confirm, Center: nothing scrolls, the large figure reads RECORDED, no pipeline contacted, and the legend reads Next press: Publish responder handoff. Center publishes: HTTP 200, the handoff's responder, facts and next step clear the key bar under the rollback steps. Down lands on Incident evidence: 50.0% over 58 namings in 1160 synthetic labelled cases.

beats.narration_text: The ring jumps to the nearest control in the direction pressed, and the label at the bottom right names it. Center opens delivery velocity, and Back now reads: back to the wall.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Right to Delivery velocity, Center. The panel opens and the BACK legend changes from Exit to the Fire TV launcher to Back to the wall.

beats.narration_text: Its answer is a recording, stamped offline fixture, because no GitHub token is set. Back returns to the wall, not out of the app. Cloud spend is a fixture too, marked synthetic.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Down scrolls the rest of the DORA answer into view with its OFFLINE FIXTURE stamp; the cursor stays in the panel. Back returns to the wall and the legend changes back. Right to Cloud spend, Center: the spend answer carries OFFLINE FIXTURE and says its figures are SYNTHETIC. Back to the wall.

beats.narration_text: Last, the server reports its build: the commit on the opening card, in fixture mode. The emulator footage came from C I, not a Fire TV device.
beats.visual_action: Down to How it answers, Down to Check, Center. The connection line reads GET /health returned 200, the build's short SHA, and GitHub live: no, fixture mode.
